Your daily ad workflow

Framecraft creates promotional videos from your finished images and video clips. It animates and edits the assets you supply; it does not generate new people, poses or voice recordings.

Readable editor controls

The interface uses locally bundled Open Sans with Arial as its fallback. Labels and inputs use larger text and stronger contrast. Scene buttons keep readable widths, show durations separately, and highlight the selected scene. The strip above them shows relative scene durations. Playback and guide controls sit together above the scenes. Open Sans and Arial are also available for video text; saved projects keep their chosen text style.

1. Choose a template

Use Framed Couple Video for supplied video clips with circular portrait inputs. Use Couple collage for result grids and the upload/loading sequence, Before → after for a transformation, One photo, many styles for a style sequence, Three-step demo for upload/choose/reveal, or Result showcase to lead with your finished work. Step 3 and step 6 show the controls relevant to the selected template.

2. Set size, branding and timing

Step 2 offers portrait 1080 × 1920, square 1080 × 1080, landscape 1920 × 1080, and custom dimensions. Custom sizes must be even whole numbers from 256 to 3840, with a maximum area of 8.29 megapixels. Layouts fit without stretching; extra space uses your background color.

Open Scene durations to change each image-template scene in seconds. The timeline shows the resulting total and lets you jump to a scene. Choosing a preset duration resets the current template’s custom scene timings. For framed videos, use the scene duration/trim controls on each clip and the separate end-card duration in step 7.

Brand presets save your logo, app name, CTA, fonts, colors and watermark. Save a named preset, then apply it to another project without replacing its photos or timing.

3. Add and position assets

Upload up to 12 finished result images for image templates, or up to 6 video clips for the framed template. Add original/partner photos when the chosen template uses them. Drag result images to reorder. Framed scenes have their own headings, portraits, trim and reorder controls.

In Crop & position images, select an image, set zoom from 100–300%, and move the image with horizontal/vertical positions. At 0% the crop uses the left/top edge; at 100% it uses the right/bottom edge. Check the actual stage preview, since different templates use different image boxes. The small crop preview shows the selected output aspect ratio. Reset crop restores the centered image. Crop settings travel with the asset.

Trim is non-destructive: set start and end positions, play the selected range, then choose Use selected range. Source clip audio is muted; add music and voiceover in step 8.

4. Style text, watermark and animations

Step 4 controls the main text: font, alignment, colors and outline. Captions can be entered with start/end times or imported from SRT. Step 5 styles the watermark independently. Step 6 controls motion, loading effects and framed appearance, including a separate upload heading style.

In step 7, upload a logo and optional end-card image or video. End-card entrance, logo motion, CTA motion and particles are independent controls. An uploaded card’s existing text and logo are baked into that media and cannot be separately animated. The dedicated end-card SFX stays anchored to the end-card start, even when scene timing changes.

5. Finish the audio

Step 8 has separate background music, voiceover and timed SFX. Music supports volume, source offset and looping. Voiceover supports start time, source offset, length and volume. A length of 0 means use the remaining source audio. Add fade-in/out for music and voiceover, and enable music reduction under the voiceover. A ducking level of 25% means the music drops to one quarter of its selected volume while voiceover plays, with short transitions.

Use main Play to hear the mixed audio. SFX timing buttons for upload/loading/reveal follow Couple collage’s current scene timing; they are disabled for templates that do not use that sequence. Manual SFX/caption times remain absolute when you change the video duration. Automatic speech transcription and built-in music libraries are not included.

6. Save, undo and share projects

OptionWhat it keeps
Autosave / Save projectSettings, images and attached video/audio on this browser through local storage. Open Projects & recovery to choose another saved project, create a new project or save a copy.
Undo / RedoUp to 30 editing snapshots during this session, including media references. Click the toolbar controls or use Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z outside a text field. Text fields retain their normal typing undo.
JSON project backupImages, settings and media metadata. Video and audio files must be reattached.
Complete project packageA ZIP containing the editable project plus all attached original video/audio files. Missing attachments must be reattached before packaging. Package limit: 1 GB.

To hand work to a colleague, download Complete project package and send that ZIP. They open it using Open project. Imported backups and packages become separate local projects, so an existing saved project is preserved. Local autosaves and brand libraries are specific to the browser/origin; they do not sync between accounts or between local and online copies. Browser data clearing can remove them. Keep packages for independent backups.

7. Review and export

Preview guides shade conservative margins where platform UI might cover your content. They are estimates, not official placement guarantees. They are excluded from export. Check final placement against your intended advertising platform.

Precise MP4 · fixed 30 fps encodes every frame at a fixed timestamp and mixes audio offline. Supported codecs and dimensions are checked before export. Use a browser with H.264/AAC encoding support. If unsupported, choose Browser recording; that mode uses real-time recording with a variable frame rate, and the tab must remain visible. The export can be cancelled without changing the project. Failures show a reason and restore the controls.

Batch export creates one ZIP with selected portrait, square and landscape sizes and up to 20 variations per selected size. Variations rotate result images or framed scene order. Add one hook per line to cycle the text; for framed videos, batch hooks replace the scene headings in that variation. The original edit is restored afterwards. The ZIP is capped at 512 MB; if cancelled or interrupted, completed videos are packaged as a partial batch.

Offline use

Open the local dist/index.html in a compatible browser, or serve the same folder locally. All scripts, fonts and codec-container helpers are bundled with the app; media stays in the browser. Browser capabilities still apply offline. Keep the entire folder, including vendor, together. For a colleague, share the updated dist.zip along with any complete project packages.

Recommended daily routine: open a saved project or package → apply your brand → replace assets → adjust crop and timing → check text, guides and audio → save a complete package → export the selected sizes and variations.
